spec.name: sentiment_ranking
spec.notes: Backtest based on sentiment revisions as described in the blog.

claim.text: A strategy based on sentiment revisions, ranking assets daily and long-short the top and bottom 20% of the universe. The Sharpe ratio is 12.82, with low volatility and drawdowns.

exhibits.summary: On the sealed period, traded as live (strict data, 10 bps, at least one bar of lag), the Sharpe ratio is -0.89 against 12.82 in research, a gap of +13.72.
The log shows a single trial, so there is no selection to correct for.

Delaying the signal by 1 more bar moves the Sharpe ratio from 12.82 to 0.66 (change -12.16). The strategy already trades a bar after its signal, so this measures how fast the signal fades, not look-ahead.
On the full universe the Sharpe ratio is 12.61 against 12.82 as submitted; the strategy never saw 38 delisted assets.
At 10 bps the Sharpe ratio is 11.10 (as submitted, 0 bps: 12.82); it breaks even at 73.9 bps with daily turnover 0.20.

charges.argument: The holdout test shows that the Sharpe ratio on the sealed period is -0.89, which is significantly lower than the research Sharpe ratio of 12.82, indicating overfitting.

rebuttals.argument: The holdout test shows that the Sharpe ratio on the sealed period is -0.89, which is significantly lower than the research Sharpe ratio of 12.82. This indicates overfitting, as the strategy fails to replicate its performance in a live, strict mode with realistic costs.

verdict.opinion: The holdout test shows a significant drop in Sharpe ratio from 12.82 to -0.89, indicating overfitting and lookahead bias. The strategy fails to replicate performance in live conditions, suggesting the claimed results are not real.
